newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: IMF's Fischer urges single Uzbek exchange rate.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Fischer urges single Uzbek exchange rate.

text.p: Stanley Fischer, deputy managing director of the International Monetary Fund, said on Saturday a single exchange rate was now the most important step for the former Soviet republic of Uzbekistan.
"I think the most important step (for Uzbekistan) -- this is a single exchange rate," Fischer told a forum of bankers and businessmen in the Uzbek capital Tashkent.
The IMF suspended a $185 million loan to the former Soviet republic late last year over foreign exchange controls and missed inflation targets.
Fischer had been invited by the government to try and improve relations with the IMF. He met Uzbek President Islam Karimov and other senior officials on Friday.
Diplomatic sources said foreign exchange controls had been likely to top the agenda in the meetings, but Fischer said exchange controls were not discussed.
Asked how long it would be before exchange controls might be removed, Fischer told Reuters, "It could be next year, it could be later this year, but we haven't really discussed that."
Fischer said the Fund would continue to work with Uzbekistan.
"We will work with the government on how to make possible for the government to carry out the agreement which was reached in December 1995," Fischer said.
Rustam Azimov, chairman of the National Bank for Foreign Economic Activity, told the forum, "Mr Fischer laid before us very serious and deep questions to which today we have no answers."

Earlier this week, business figures and diplomats said they doubted the visit would see any quick end to exchange controls, saying the government would wait to see the outcome of this year's cotton and wheat harvest.
Desperate for cash to bail out the troubled agriculture sector, the government imposed the exchange controls late last year following disastrous harvests in 1996.
The controls have created a flourishing black market in dollars, with the so-called "bazaar rate" at around 142 sums to the dollar, way above the official exchange rate of 59.66 sums to the dollar.
But Uzbek Finance Minister Bakhtier Khamidov told the forum, "I think that in November or December we will make progress and return to macro-economic targets.
There is a routine IMF mission visit under way in Uzbekistan which will last until May 13.
